title: RTP RFC2198: Tap primary encoding payload instead
description:
When RFC 2198 Redundant Audio Data is being used, de-encapsulate
the primary encoding from the redundant headers when sending
information to the RTP tap, by adjusting the start offset, length,
and payload type.

The payload with the RFC 2198 headers will never play back in the
RTP Player, but the de-encapsulated primary encoding might.

Actually handling redundant audio or ULPFEC (RFC 5109) sent in
RFC 2198 encapsuation would be considerably more work.

This has a preference because someone may want to export the
encapsulated raw payload with the secondary codecs as well on
occasion instead of only the primary codec.

Note that WebRTC/Chromium sends nonstandard RFC 2198 packets when
using video and ULPFEC, sending the FEC as separate RTP packets
with duplicate sequence numbers, instead of as secondary encodings:
https://bugs.chromium.org/p/webrtc/issues/detail?id=9188
https://bugs.chromium.org/p/webrtc/issues/detail?id=12530
https://bugs.chromium.org/p/webrtc/issues/detail?id=1467
Though it treats actual redundant audio in a RFC-compliant way:
https://bugs.chromium.org/p/webrtc/issues/detail?id=11640
